title: Tercer condicional: If I had known…

rule.title: Third conditional
rule.explanation:
El tercer condicional imagina un pasado diferente, algo que ya no se puede cambiar: «If» + past perfect, «would have» + participio:
- «If Sam hadn't played that gig, the producer wouldn't have heard him.» (si no hubiera tocado, no le habría oído)
- «If I had known, I would have helped you.»

Sirve para hablar de lo que pudo ser y para lamentarse. En la otra parte también pueden ir «could have» o «might have»:
- «If we had left earlier, we could have caught the train.»

Contracciones habituales: «If I'd known…» = «If I had known»; «I would've» = «I would have». En la conversación «would have» suena /wʊdəv/.

Compara los tres:
- 1.º (real, futuro): «If he goes, he'll be famous.»
- 2.º (imaginario, presente): «If he went, he'd be famous.»
- 3.º (imaginario, pasado): «If he had gone, he would have been famous.»

Ojo: «'d» puede ser «had» o «would». Después de «if» es «had»; delante de «have», «would»: «If I'd known, I'd have come» = «If I had known, I would have come».

rows: If he hadn't come, we wouldn't have met.
We could have caught the train.
